items.title: Element delivery is not recorded
items.whyItMatters: The working group argues without data.
items.opportunity: Record each element on a two-minute form in theatre for every resection.

items.title: Compliance definition for non-applicable elements
items.whyItMatters: Counting non-applicable elements as delivered inflates compliance (claim c3).
items.opportunity: All-or-none over applicable elements with written applicability rules.

items.title: Confounding by emergency surgery
items.whyItMatters: Emergency cases have less compliance and more infection (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Adjust for emergency status and contamination and report elective and emergency results separately.

items.title: Post-discharge infections missed for patients who live alone
items.whyItMatters: Almost half of infections appear after discharge (claim c2) and unreachable patients are older and live alone.
items.opportunity: Up to three call attempts and a clinic check for patients not reached.

errorsFound: One appraisal score (140) was outside 0 to 100 and one lead gave its year as a boolean; both are stored as unknown.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a prospective observational study with applicability-based compliance, adjustment for emergency status and complete post-discharge follow-up.
summary: Four gaps; missing element data, the compliance definition and confounding are high severity.
